title: Tech company enters the US

source.book: IIM Lucknow Casebook 2025-26, EY-Parthenon interview experiences

prompt: A tech-based company wants to enter the US market. Give a framework for entry.

facts.reveal: A tech-based company that develops apps.

facts.asks: Which part of the framework to focus on
facts.reveal: No, go ahead and tell me the important points.

crux.statement: A small app firm cannot take on the US market head-on. The stronger answer enters through backend support or services for US firms rather than independently, and says why that fits a small company.
crux.clue: The interviewer wants "the important points", not a full framework: the round tests whether the candidate prioritises quickly.

paths: Why enter → where and whom to serve → how to enter (services or business-to-business, partnership, own product)
Any short, prioritised structure that uses the fact that the company is small

wrongTurns.text: Proposing a direct consumer launch with heavy marketing spend

close.condition: The candidate has named a mode of entry.
close.prompt: Summarise your recommended mode of entry, your reasons and the main risk.

anchors.s5: Generic framework that never uses the facts.
anchors.s7: Clear structure and a mode, with some link to size.
anchors.s9: Brief and prioritised; a low-risk entry justified by small scale; names what would need checking before going further.

verifierFlags.text: The write-up does not record the interviewer's reaction to the answer, and the same interview went on to an ATM guesstimate and a kulfi-stall case.
verifierFlags.decision: Run as a 10-minute framework drill. The follow-on cases are not built for the pilot.
